intro: You're searching for an eco home architect near you because you want a home that's genuinely low-energy, comfortable and kind to the planet. You need someone local who understands insulation, airtightness, renewables and sustainable materials, and who can turn your ideas into a practical design. We can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an eco home architect usually need
need_lead: Most people want a local architect who can design a home that is energy-efficient, healthy to live in and built with sustainable materials.
needs: You are planning a new build and want a design that keeps heat in, uses little energy and makes the most of natural light and solar gain.
You are extending or renovating an existing home and want to improve its energy performance without losing character or comfort.
You need help choosing insulation, airtightness measures and renewable technologies such as heat pumps or solar panels.
You want to reduce the whole-life carbon of your home, from the materials used to how it will perform over time.
You are looking for someone local who can visit the site, understand the orientation and surroundings, and guide you through planning and building regulations.
context_heading: Understanding who can call themselves an architect
context: "Architect" is a protected title in the UK. Only people on the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register can call themselves architects, and they must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance. Many practices are also RIBA Chartered Practices. Architectural designers and technologists can do excellent work too, but they are not registered architects, so it is worth knowing which you are hiring.

Before you appoint anyone, check the ARB register and ask for a written appointment that sets out services, fees and responsibilities. Building regulations approval, planning permission and party wall matters are separate processes that your architect can help you navigate.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Whether you are building a new home, extending, or renovating an existing property, and roughly how big the project is.
Your priorities for the eco aspects, such as high insulation, airtightness, a heat pump, solar panels, or natural materials.
Any planning stage you have reached, such as whether you have outline permission or are starting from scratch.
Your budget range for the design work and construction, so the professional can tailor their quote.
Where the property is located, so we can introduce you to someone who works in your area.
Any specific sustainable materials or technologies you are keen to use, or any you want to avoid.
questions: Are you a registered architect with the Architects Registration Board, and can you provide your registration number?
How will you approach the whole-life carbon of my home, from materials to energy use?
What experience do you have with low-energy design and renewable technologies like heat pumps?
Can you explain how you will ensure good insulation and airtightness in the design?
What is your process for managing planning permission and building regulations approval?
What are your fees, and what do they include?

faqs.q: Do I need a registered architect for an eco home?
faqs.a: Not always, but only registered architects can call themselves architects. Architectural designers and technologists can also design eco homes, so it is worth checking their qualifications and experience. You can check the ARB register to confirm someone is a registered architect.

faqs.q: How can an architect help make my home more eco-friendly?
faqs.a: An eco home architect can design with high insulation, airtightness, renewables and sustainable materials to reduce energy use and carbon. They can also advise on grants that may support upgrades and help you navigate planning and building regulations.

faqs.q: What should I look for in an eco home architect near me?
faqs.a: Look for someone local who understands your site and has experience with low-energy design. Check they are a registered architect if they use that title, and ask about their approach to insulation, airtightness and renewables. A written appointment setting out services and fees is essential.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a specific architect?
faqs.a: We introduce you to a suitable UK professional based on your needs, and they will quote you directly. We do not recommend or endorse individual professionals, and we cannot promise any particular outcome for your project. You should satisfy yourself that the professional is right for you.
